# evaluate


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Evaluation here only needs `predict(state, questions)` returning answers
in the Jev schema, so the same functions score a sysone
[`Decider`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#decider),
a
[`GlinerDecider`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/gliner_backend.html#glinerdecider),
a `laya.Agent` (whose result wraps the answers in `{"answers": ...}`) or
a client of any `/v1/systemone` endpoint, with the definitions of Laya’s
evaluation cell. A small trained model to score:

``` python
from sysone.data import TypedDecisions
from sysone.learner import decision_learner
```

``` python
recs = [json.loads(l) for l in Path("fixtures/typed_decisions_tiny.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
data = TypedDecisions.from_records(recs[:15], calib=0)
torch.manual_seed(0)
learn = decision_learner(data, "fixtures/tiny-modernbert", train="full", preset="cpu", loss="soft_ce")
learn.fit(3, lr=2e-3)
jev = learn.decider()
```

Any metric of the [metrics](04a_metrics.ipynb) notebook works here too,
from the answers alone: `metrics=` adds a column for each, computed on
[`Preds.from_answers`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/metrics.html#preds.from_answers):

``` python
from sysone.metrics import F1Score, CohenKappa, Metric, noul_auroc
```

``` python
more = evaluate(jev, recs[15:], metrics=[F1Score("weighted"), Metric(CohenKappa("quadratic"), qtype="score"), noul_auroc])
test_eq(more["accuracy"], res["accuracy"])
{k: round(more[k], 3) for k in ("accuracy", "macro_f1", "f1_score_weighted", "cohen_kappa_quadratic_score", "noul_auroc")}
```

### typed-decisions

[`typed_decisions_report`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/evaluate.html#typed_decisions_report)
scores the test split, 400 cases and 2,000 decisions, per workflow, next
to the reference rows of the dataset card, all measured on the same
split. Read 0.52 as the floor and 0.735, the teacher’s self-agreement,
as saturation; the card’s advice is to read KL and Brier as well, since
a prior that ignores the input has the best ECE.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a

## Behaviour probes

[semantic-browser](https://github.com/koriym/semantic-browser) drove a
hypermedia agent with Laya zero-shot and documented four failures, with
deterministic repeats.
[`behaviors`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/evaluate.html#behaviors)
turns them into regression probes; each returns whether it passed and
what it saw, and a model should be expected to fail some of them until
trained for it:

- **negation**: an option whose description says it *cannot* serve the
  goal (“cannot be used to find the reviewers of a specific manuscript”)
  won with 0.79 for a goal it excludes; the correct option must win, and
  adding the negation to an option must lower its probability;
- **uri**: a URI in the state (`"At /index. Goal: list all books."`)
  flipped the winner to the `index` link, 0.912, which lost to `books`
  without it; the argmax must be `books` both ways;
- **candidate set**: the winner between two options changed when a
  third, irrelevant one was removed (books 0.627 with `index` present,
  authors 0.601 without); the order of the two must not flip;
- **confidence**: zero-shot confidence did not track correctness (a
  wrong answer at 0.96, a right one at 0.29); on records with gold, the
  probe reports the AUROC of
  [`answer_confidence`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/core.html#answer_confidence)
  against correctness, which should clear 0.5 by a margin.

The first probe’s descriptions are English renderings of the Japanese
ones in the semantic-browser trace; the others use its English strings.
